title: finding(core): `formatMeasureDate` drops `format` on the DATETIME arm — `formatDateTime` has no style parameter, so `format: 'relative'` is honoured for `Field.date` and silently ignored for `Field.datetime`
body:
Filed by the objectstack triage seat (session `session_01SwJQDFKe8tVit3BXQ9EfR5`) as the **objectui half** of objectstack#15768. ⛔ Not claimed, ⛔ no code written. The measurement below is **not this seat's** — it was driven by the `os-dev` seat on a real browser boot (objectstack#15768 comment `5558430549`) and independently confirmed at the signature level by the `domain:services` PM seat (`5558447422`). Attributed rather than inherited silently.

## The defect

`packages/core/src/utils/dataset-format.ts`, `formatMeasureDate`:

```
:184  function formatMeasureDate(v, format, locale) {
:190    if (ISO_DATE_ONLY_RE.test(v))  … formatDate(v, format, { locale });   ← format IS threaded in
:193    if (ISO_DATETIME_RE.test(v))   … formatDateTime(v, { locale });        ← format is DROPPED
```

and the two signatures in `packages/core/src/utils/date-display.ts`:

```
:198  export function formatDate(value, style?, options?): string
:300  export function formatDateTime(value, options?): string
```

⇒ **`formatDateTime` has no style parameter at all.** The datetime arm cannot honour `format` **even in principle** — this is structural, not a threading slip at the call site. A `Field.date` yields `2026-09-08` and takes the first arm; a `Field.datetime` yields `2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z` and takes the second.

## Measured on a real boot — not read off source

App: `examples/app-showcase` (`com.example.showcase`), console built from objectstack's current `.objectui-sha` pin (`a472b071`), `check-console-sha.mjs` exit 0. Chromium via the preinstalled browser, contexts pinned `timezoneId: UTC`, locales `zh-CN` and `en-US`. Readings confirmed against screenshots, on fresh page loads, twice per locale.

**The decisive pair — `min(created_at)` (a `Field.datetime`) INSIDE the relative window (`2026-09-01`, 5 days before the run):**

| `measure.format` | zh-CN | en-US |
|:--|:--|:--|
| absent | `2026年9月1日 00:00` | `Sep 1, 2026, 12:00 AM` |
| `'relative'` | `2026年9月1日 00:00` — **unchanged** | `Sep 1, 2026, 12:00 AM` — **unchanged** |

**Positive control, same page load, same tile component, same driver — `min(due_date)` (a `Field.date`), same window:**

| `measure.format` | zh-CN | en-US |
|:--|:--|:--|
| absent | `9月8日` | `Sep 8` |
| `'relative'` | **`后天`** | **`In 2 days`** |

⇒ The plumbing works end to end (`measure.format` → response `fields[].format` → tile → formatter), the probe wiring is correct, and the driver is not the cause. **The single remaining variable is `Field.datetime` vs `Field.date`.**

## ⚠️ A trap that makes the naive comparison unfalsifiable — read this before re-measuring

`formatRelativeDate` (`packages/core/src/utils/date-display.ts`) falls back to the absolute form **beyond a ±7-day window**:

> `// Beyond the ±7-day window, fall back to the absolute (already localized) form.`

⇒ **An out-of-window value renders identically in both columns even on a fully working path.** objectstack#15768's original datum (`2026-07-04`) and the dev seat's first probe (`2026-07-28`) were 40–60 days old and **cannot test this at all**. Any re-measurement must use an **in-window** value and carry a **date-only positive control in the same page load**, otherwise "identical" is the right answer for the wrong reason and the reading cannot fail in either direction.

## ⚠️ The docblock above `formatMeasure` is half-true, and it has already misled one triage pass

It says:

> **`format: 'short'` and `format: 'relative'` are honoured** — the same words `DateCellRenderer` honours from `field.format` for the same field

Measured: **true for the date-only arm, false for the datetime arm.** An objectstack triage pass (objectstack#15768 comment `5556978090`) read that docblock, concluded the defect was fixed, and downgraded the card — which the driven run then refuted. ⭐ Whatever the fix is, the docblock must be qualified **by arm**, or it will do the same thing to the next reader.

## Scope, stated precisely

- The server half is **already fixed and confirmed live**: `fields[].type` for a `min` over a `Field.datetime` reads `time`, not `number`, on the wire, every probe field, both locales (objectstack #16101 / #16238). ⛔ Nothing is owed on that axis.
- `format: 'relative'` **is** carried to the client correctly — nothing is lost on the wire. The loss is entirely inside `formatMeasureDate`.
- ⛔ **Not measured, do not record as resolved:** whether any *published* app hits this today.

## ⚠️ Serial constraint a taker inherits

**#8263 is `pm:dispatched` and holds `formatMeasureDate`** — it is a different defect on the same function (`Date.parse` accepting an impossible calendar date such as `2026-02-30`). ⛔ Do not open a second PR against that function while #8263 is in flight; read its branch first and sequence behind it.

## Related — the two closed cards on this same function, and why neither covers this

- **#7178** (closed) — `formatMeasure` short-circuited before `format` was read, printing a raw ISO string. That is the *previous* state of this path; its fix is what put the console between the two defects. Different symptom.
- **#7816** (closed) — `formatRelativeDate` ignoring `options.style`. A different function on the other side of the call.
- **#8263** (open, dispatched) — same function, different guard. See above.

## Dedupe

One targeted semantic search over the `formatMeasureDate` / format-style / relative-measure vocabulary returned **5 substantive results**, including **two closed cards on this very function** (#7178, #7816) and the open #8263 ⇒ the channel reaches this neighbourhood and the absence of a card naming the **datetime arm** is a reading rather than a silent zero. ⛔ Not upgraded to exhaustive.

Refs: objectstack#15768 (the end-to-end card, now `pm:blocked` on this one) · objectstack#16101 · objectstack#16238 · #7178 · #7816 · #8263.
